cells.tense: The yield is in, and you are the one at the table dividing it.
cells.ask: Write one page listing who helped you get here and what each is owed, then hand it to one of them.
cells.core:
Something you tended has come in, and you are the one at the table dividing it. The work was slow and mostly unwatched, and you know the pace it kept, so what leaves your hands is measured rather than scattered. People feel the evenness of it without being told, which is why the shares hold.

There is more room in this than you are using. The same care that keeps the shares squared can carry one more reckoning, and the season is still open. Keep the habit and turn it once toward the people whose part in this has gone uncounted — a page is enough, in your own hand, and the fairness you already run is the whole method.
cells.sheetLine: You divide what came in by what actually went into it.
cells.verb: Weighing what came in and what each hand is owed for it
cells.place: Where shares are recounted and proportion is recalibrated until it squares again

cells.tense: You are guarding against a shortage that has not happened yet, while the table is still full.
cells.ask: Before you plan the next thing tonight, sit down for ten minutes with what is already finished.
cells.core:
The abundance is real and you are already bracing against its loss. Every gift gets turned over for the catch it could hide; you count who might take a share before anyone asks. Care that runs ahead of what has actually happened stops being care and becomes watchfulness, and watchfulness does not let anything finish ripening.

What is on the table now is yours to enjoy. The instinct to keep things even is not the problem. Where it has slipped is that you are applying it to shortages that exist only in the future you are pacing toward. Sit with what has already come in long enough to let it rest, and let the weighing wait until there is something real to weigh. Before you plan the next thing tonight, sit down for ten minutes with what is already finished.

cells.tense: The counting is the part you stopped, and the numbers you hold have gotten small.
cells.ask: Name one thing you finished well out loud, and say who helped it along.
cells.core:
The counting is the part that stopped. What you grew is still yours and the habit of growing it is intact, but somewhere the weighing fell out of use, and since then you have been keeping your holdings small — less of it, you seem to figure, means less to account for. Fewer things finished, fewer people let close to what does finish.

What is missing is not the growing. It is the direction that says which light to move toward, and that comes back by naming something already complete. One thing you finished well, said out loud to someone who would not be surprised to hear it, with the people who helped it named alongside. One thing only. The rest of the table can wait until you are used to sitting at it again.
cells.sheetLine: You kept the growing and quietly dropped the counting.

cells.tense: You are already balancing what people around you can carry, and calling it the situation.
cells.ask: Tell one person plainly that a thing you do for them is a choice you are making and not a duty.
cells.core:
People around you are steadier for what you do — the way you measure before decisions harden, the questions you ask so nobody gets squeezed. You call it keeping the peace, or being practical, or simply the shape of the week. The fairness is running well and it is running below where your attention lives, so it gets described as something that happens rather than something you do.

Keep holding the room if you want to. What you are free to drop is the telling-yourself that you had no say in it. Choosing is what makes it fair. Without choosing it is only a habit wearing fairness like a coat. Tell one person plainly that a thing you do for them is something you are choosing.
